Our approach to R&D

Position Summary
GSK's Enterprise AI team builds AI solutions that prove value fast and scale to production. You will lead the Forward Deployed Engineering (FDE) function — the front of the Enterprise AI delivery pipeline that proves AI ideas with the business through PoCs, PoVs, MVPs and, where appropriate, first production versions, before handing proven solutions off to the Solutions Engineer for scale-up. This pattern is proven by AI-native companies such as Anthropic, Palantir and OpenAI, and this role brings that model to GSK.

You will hold direct line management of the FDE team (Staff, Lead, Senior, and Forward Deployed Engineers), setting FDE strategy and engagement priorities, owning Director-level BU sponsor relationships, and representing Enterprise AI on FDE matters to GSK leadership — while continuing to contribute technically at the frontier of AI-augmented engineering, where humans steer and agents execute. Enterprise AI's credibility with the business depends on engineers who can land inside BU problems, prove value quickly, and hand off cleanly; you will build and lead the function that makes this happen.

Responsibilities
This role will provide YOU the opportunity to lead key activities to progress YOUR career. These responsibilities include some of the following:

- Lead the Forward Deployed Engineering function — strategy, structure, hiring, development, and standards for the function.

- Hire, mentor, and develop the FDE team — creating development paths from G8 through to G5.

- Set the standards for AI-native engineering practice within the function — agent workflows, prompt and pattern libraries, handoff hygiene.

- Own relationships with Director and Senior Director-level BU sponsors across business units that bring AI use cases to Enterprise AI.

- Take on the most strategic FDE engagements personally — the ones that set precedents for the function.

- Make and defend portfolio-level kill/continue decisions across FDE engagements with BU and Enterprise AI leadership.

- Coordinate with the Solutions Engineering and Operations Engineering functions on the delivery pipeline; represent FDE in Enterprise AI leadership forums.

- Influence vendor strategy and tooling choices for AI-native engineering practice within Enterprise AI.

- Ensure the FDE function operates within Code Orange, Responsible AI, and Accountability Report governance from the prototype stage onward.

- Provide regular reporting to Enterprise AI leadership on FDE function performance — engagement pipeline, outcomes, team development, and capacity.

Why You?
Basic Qualification
We are seeking professionals with the following required skills and qualifications to help us achieve our goals

- PhD or master’s degree in computer science, Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience.

- 12 or more years of experience in software engineering and AI/ML engineering, with significant time leading senior engineering teams or functions.

- Demonstrated experience taking AI ideas from sketch to working software at speed, in customer-facing engineering roles.

- Strong technical depth in GenAI patterns: agents, multi-agent orchestration, RAG, and evaluation.

- Daily use of AI coding agents (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Databricks AI Assistant) as the primary mode of development.

- Experience hiring, mentoring, and developing senior engineering talent.

- Track record of representing engineering functions to senior business stakeholders.

- Hands-on experience with Openclaw/Hermes agents.

Preferred Qualification
If you have the following characteristics, it would be a plus

- Prior leadership experience at an AI-native company (Anthropic, Palantir, OpenAI, or similar) — Head of Forward Deployed Engineering, Director of Solutions, or equivalent.

- Experience in regulated industries (pharma, healthcare, financial services).

- Experience setting AI engineering standards at organizational scale.

- Clinical development experience.

There are a lot of AI startups out there right now, all claiming they're doing something different. But how many are actually building technology that businesses genuinely need?

This company is taking an interesting approach to that.

They're focused on industries where people are still spending ridiculous amounts of time working through documents, managing spreadsheets, processing emails and dealing with admin that really shouldn't need so much human involvement.

The aim is to change that by building AI powered systems that take on the repetitive work and make these processes far more efficient. And that's where you come in. They're looking for a Founding Forward Deployed Engineer to join a small engineering team and help turn some pretty complicated business problems into working software.

You will be getting close to the problems themselves, understanding how things currently work and figuring out where AI can actually make a difference.

It's a hands on engineering role, where you'll be working across AI, backend systems, integrations, data and whatever else is needed to get something working. There won't always be a clear brief or someone telling you exactly how to approach a problem, so you'll need to be comfortable figuring things out for yourself.

The good thing is, you'll actually get to see what happens when your work goes live. You're not spending months building something without knowing whether it's going to be useful.

It's still early days, but there's a clear plan for where they want to take the business, along with the investment and backing to make it happen.

The engineering team is small, which means you'll be working closely with senior technical leadership, having a say in how things are built and taking on far more responsibility than you would in a larger company.

There's also meaningful equity on offer, so you'll have a stake in what you're helping to create. It's not going to suit everyone. There's a lot to figure out, things will change quickly and some weeks will be pretty demanding. But if you like the idea of joining something early, getting stuck into difficult engineering problems and having the freedom to build things your way, there's a lot to like here.

What are they looking for?

A strong software engineer who's comfortable working across the stack and isn't restricted to one language.

Someone who's already built and shipped AI applications into production.

Experience working in environments where you've had to take ownership and figure things out without much hand nholding.

An interest in building products from scratch and solving problems that don't always have an obvious answer.

You don't need to have 'Forward Deployed Engineer' on your CV. What's more important is that you enjoy getting close to the problem, working out what needs building and then actually building it.

Title: AI Engineer – Remote
Description:
Job title: AI Engineer
Report to: Head of AI
Location: Remote within the UK, with regular time on site with clients and our group companies, typically four to eight days a month
Hours: Monday to Friday, 09:00 to 18:00 (40 hours a week)

About us

Owlis is a UK IT managed services group, backed by private equity, that grows by bringing established regional IT providers together on one platform. Each business keeps its own name and its local relationships. Behind it sits one set of systems, one set of policies, and a group with the depth to support it properly. Together, we look after small and medium-sized businesses across the UK with managed IT, cybersecurity, and AI and transformation services.

About the role

When a client decides to use AI, someone has to build it, connect it to their systems and make it safe. This role works directly with clients, often on site, to build and deploy AI assistants, agents and automations on their data, then hands them over in a state our service desks can support.

Core systems

- Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry and Azure AI Search

- Copilot Studio and Power Platform

- Python and/or C#, Git, Azure DevOps or GitHub

- Microsoft Graph and client system APIs

- HaloPSA for project time, tasks and handover to support

What you will be doing

Build and deploy

- Design, build and deploy LLM applications for clients: assistants, retrieval over documents, agents and AI-assisted workflows

- Integrate with client systems through APIs, with scoped permissions

- Choose models and services to fit the client’s needs and budget, with the Head of AI

- Use version control, testing and deployment pipelines for everything we ship

Forward deployed with clients

- Work on site or remotely alongside client staff to understand the work and test with real users

- Explain what was built, how to use it and its limits in plain English

- Gather feedback after go-live and improve the build

Quality, security and support

- Build evaluation sets and monitoring for accuracy, cost and usage

- Apply least privilege, secrets management and client data handling rules

- Write handover documentation and runbooks for our service desks

- Record AI systems in our register with owners and risk ratings

Reuse and internal work

- Contribute connectors, templates and prompt and evaluation sets to a shared library

- Build internal AI tools for our own group companies

- Log time and tasks in HaloPSA

Outcomes and KPIs

- In the first 90 days: several client builds running, with reusable components (connectors, prompt and evaluation sets) in our shared library.

- By 6 months: 10 or more repeatable propositions delivered and rolled out to clients, each with standard scope, testing and handover.

- By 12 months: revenue targets met on the first 10 propositions, with more in flight.

Competencies

- Clear evidence of building and shipping LLM applications to real users, with integrations and testing described

- Explains retrieval or tool design, prompt and model choices, cost control and failure handling from first-hand work, and is honest about mistakes

- Builds integrations and automations with error handling, logging, least privilege and scoped service accounts, and uses vendor features before custom code

- Listens to clients and gets examples, explains plainly what the tool can and can’t do, and agrees a fix and a follow-up

- Designs a clear architecture (sources, indexing, permissions-aware retrieval, model, interface), talks through trade-offs and adapts when requirements change

- Uses security-trimmed retrieval, a tested evaluation set with agreed accuracy, and monitoring with a feedback loop, keeping data in the client’s tenant where possible

- Owns mistakes and fixes them, follows through and manages expectations when things slip

Essential skills and experience

- Has built and shipped applications using large language models, such as assistants, retrieval over documents (RAG) or agents

- Writes production-quality code in Python or C#, with version control and testing

- Has integrated AI or applications with business systems through APIs, for example Microsoft Graph, a CRM or a ticketing tool

- Builds with security and data protection in mind: least privilege, secrets handling and safe use of client data

- Can work directly with client users to understand a problem and explain what was built

Desirable skills and experience

- Experience with Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, Azure AI Search or Copilot Studio

- Has set up evaluation for AI outputs (test sets, accuracy measures, monitoring)

- Power Platform, Logic Apps or another workflow and integration tool

- Experience in an IT managed services provider or a client-facing engineering role

- Microsoft Azure AI Engineer Associate (AI-102) or similar certification

- Infrastructure as code or CI/CD pipelines in Azure

Development

We expect the role to grow into a senior or lead AI engineer as the practice scales. Certification (for example AI-102) is supported where it fits the work.

Our recruitment process

Our process usually has four stages:

- A short pre-screening call with our HR / Recruitment team.

- A competency interview with the Head of AI / Operations Director

- A live system design exercise with a client scenario and a technical assessment

- A short final call with an Owlis Group executive, after which we aim to make an offer.

Any offer is conditional on two satisfactory professional references from employers named on your CV (with a work email address for each), proof of your right to work in the UK and a basic DBS check, because the role has privileged access to client systems and data. We are unable to offer visa sponsorship.

Please note that this is a job advertisement rather than a full job description. The complete job description will be shared with you alongside your contract of employment.

Equal opportunities

The Owlis Group is an equal opportunities employer. We welcome applications from everyone and make recruitment decisions on the basis of skills, experience and potential, regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage or civil partnership, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation. Title: AI Engineer
Description:
About the role
We already run two kinds of agent alongside our teams. AI agents diagnose performance problems and tell people the root cause. Rule-based agents recommend marketing actions to our advertising teams. The quality of their decisions shows up directly in our revenue.
Next, both take a greater role in the day-to-day running of our lead generation business, moving from recommending, to acting with a person's approval, to acting on their own where it is safe. We need an engineer to build agents that are dependable in production, measurable, and safe to trust with more.
This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll own agents end to end, from understanding the workflow to running them in production, alongside our existing AI engineer, data scientists, product managers and the people who use the agents every day. Today we use Claude and open-weight models such as GLM, chosen per task on quality and cost, on an agent framework we build ourselves.

What you'll do
Build agents

- Start from the workflow. Sit with the operators, map how the work is actually done, and build for that, not for the process as documented.

- Build on shared rules. Rule-based and LLM agents that call shared, versioned rules and tools, not logic hard-coded inside each agent.

- Connect them to the business. Using our data warehouse, internal services, and the APIs into the systems agents act in.

- Turn outputs into results people trust. Structured outputs, validation and clear application logic.

Make them safe to trust

- Log every decision. Each action records its context, what was chosen, and whether a person accepted or overrode it, so agents can be evaluated and improved.

- Build the path to autonomy. Per decision, agents move from recommend, to act with approval, to act alone. Our data scientists propose the bar from agreement and override data and point people in the business sign it off; you build the mechanism that enforces it on our shared agent framework, with permissions and guardrails in the code, not the prompt.

- Evaluate behaviour, not just code. Test sets, agreement with expert operators, and evaluation before and after every change.

- Run what you ship. Tracing, failure handling, and tracking quality, latency and cost. There's no on-call rota.

What we're offering you:

- Summer Fridays

- Competitive holiday benefits - 25 days a year paid holiday, plus 8 bank holidays (increases 1 day a year up to 30 days)

- Hybrid working - 3 days a week in the office

- Closed for Christmas holidays - Extra days not taken from your annual holiday allowance.

- Work from anywhere for 2 weeks a year

- Life Assurance and Income Protection to protect your loved ones

- Benefits allowance for health, dental, and vision coverage

- Six months paid maternity leave, and one month paid paternity leave (subject to qualifying conditions) inclusive of same-sex and adoptive parents

- Defined Contribution Pension and Salary Sacrifice Scheme

- Be Well: Our award-winning wellbeing and mental health programme to support all MVFers and their families

- Family Forward support for our MVF parents and their mini-mes

- 2 charity days a year

What we're looking for

- 3+ years of engineering, including at least one LLM application or agent shipped to real users.

- Python and TypeScript: production-grade in one and productive in the other, with typed, tested code and clear interfaces. You'll work in both here.

- LLM engineering: tool calling, structured outputs, context management, and evaluating agent behaviour on representative test sets.

- Integration and operations: SQL, HTTP APIs, containers, CI/CD and a cloud platform, and debugging from logs and traces.

Nice to have

- Agents used daily by operators, with a feedback loop.

- AWS SageMaker, AWS ECS/Fargate, Terraform and CircleCI.

- Snowflake and dbt.

- Event logging for analytics or machine learning.

- Lead generation or ad tech.

How you'll work

- Commercial impact. You understand how the business creates value and use that to make better choices about what gets built, prioritised or stopped. You define the intended impact before starting, consider the cost of the work and evaluate what happened afterwards.

- Delivery and ownership. You take responsibility for outcomes and move at a pace matched to the cost of delay. You follow work through until it is delivered, handed over or deliberately stopped, and remain accountable for what happens after delivery.

- Candour and communication. You surface important information early, including when it is uncomfortable, with evidence and a view on what to do about it. You communicate what is known, assumed and uncertain in a form the audience can understand and act on.

- Making others better. You create lasting improvement in other people's and the team's work through teaching, feedback or challenge, and take challenge on your own work as readily as you give it.

- Growth and mastery. You deepen your capability through deliberate practice, feedback and experience, build the skills the work will need next, and change established practices when better approaches become available.

- Judgement under ambiguity. You make sound decisions with incomplete information and know when to act, escalate or delegate. You own what you ship regardless of how it was produced, and change position when the evidence changes.

How you'll build

- Craft and AI-native delivery. You build robust agents and AI applications, choosing the right approach for the problem, including when deterministic code is enough. You understand and can explain the evidence, assumptions, behaviour and limitations of what you build, and use AI to increase delivery speed without giving up technical ownership.

- Architecture and systems design. You design reliable systems that move agents and AI capabilities from a business problem into effective use, deciding what should be probabilistic and what deterministic. You treat data and context, security and governance, monitoring and observability, failure handling and recovery, cost, performance and lifecycle as part of the design rather than concerns added afterwards.
